name: Rack Pull Above Knee
description: The above-knee rack pull sets the starting pin height just above the knee, leaving only the final hip-extension lockout portion of the deadlift. This shortened range of motion allows for supramaximal loading and directly trains the lockout mechanics, upper back, and trapezius under heavier loads than a full deadlift allows. It is used by powerlifters to reinforce lockout strength and by athletes to build upper back and grip capacity.

execution.starting_position: Set the safety pins of a power rack just above knee height. Load the bar on the pins. Grip the bar in the same position as a conventional deadlift. The torso will be nearly vertical due to the high starting position.
execution.setup_instructions: Because of the short range of motion, loads can be significantly higher than conventional deadlift — often 110-130%. Lifting straps are commonly used.
steps: Step 1: Position yourself behind the bar with pins set just above knee height.
Step 2: Grip the bar with a double-overhand or mixed grip, brace the core.
Step 3: Drive the hips forward in a hip-extension motion, pulling the bar to lockout.
Step 4: Squeeze the glutes and stand fully erect at the top.
Step 5: Return the bar to the pins under control.
execution.breathing_instructions: Brace before each rep. Exhale at lockout.
common_mistakes: Jerking the bar off the pins — set the tension first, then pull
Not achieving full lockout at the top
Hyperextending the lower back at lockout — the goal is hip extension, not lumbar hyperextension
safety_considerations: High loads place significant demand on the grip and upper back — do not neglect warmup sets
Ensure pins are level and secure before loading
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Short range — from just above the knee to full lockout only.
coaching_cues: Take up the slack — don't yank off the pins
Drive the hips forward to lock out
